questions.title: Can a court dismiss a copyright infringement claim for fair use at the Rule 12(b)(6) stage?
questions.question_body: I'm reading Santos v. Kimmel where the Second Circuit affirmed a dismissal based on fair use at the pleading stage. I thought fair use was typically a fact-intensive affirmative defense that requires discovery to resolve. Under what circumstances is the fair use defense 'so clearly established' that it can support a Rule 12(b)(6) dismissal without factual development?

questions.title: Does the copyright holder's subjective intent matter for determining 'transformative use'?
questions.question_body: In the opinion, Santos argued that because he created the videos for a specific purpose, Kimmel's use wasn't transformative. The court cited Andy Warhol Foundation v. Goldsmith and said transformative use turns on the 'reasonable observer,' not the subjective intent of the creator or user. Can someone explain the doctrinal shift here? Why is the plaintiff's original intent irrelevant to the 'purpose and character' factor?

questions.title: Does bad faith negate the fair use defense under current Second Circuit precedent?
questions.question_body: The opinion cites Harper & Row stating that 'fair use presupposes good faith,' but then concludes that bad faith does not nullify the defense in this case. The court mentions the Supreme Court has 'distanced itself' from the Harper & Row statement. What is the current status of the good faith requirement in fair use analysis, and why didn't Kimmel's deception on Cameo defeat the defense?

questions.title: Why can't a non-party enforce Terms of Service as a third-party beneficiary?
questions.question_body: Santos tried to sue for breach of the Cameo Terms of Service even though he wasn't a party to the agreement (Kimmel was the user). The court applied Illinois law and cited a 'strong presumption against conferring benefits to noncontracting third parties.' What level of 'express declaration' is required to overcome this presumption, and why didn't the existence of third-party language in other parts of the ToS help Santos?

questions.title: What is the 'out-of-pocket loss' requirement for fraudulent inducement in New York?
questions.question_body: The court dismissed Santos's fraudulent inducement claim because he failed to allege 'actual out-of-pocket loss.' I thought fraud claims generally focus on reliance and damages resulting from the reliance. Why does New York law specifically require out-of-pocket loss rather than expectation damages or other types of harm in this context?

questions.title: Why did the court decline to decide copyright preemption of state law claims?
questions.question_body: The District Court dismissed the state law contract claims on preemption grounds, but the Second Circuit said they 'need not resolve this issue' because the claims failed under state law anyway. Is this a matter of judicial economy, or is there a specific rule about avoiding constitutional or federal preemption questions when state law grounds are sufficient?
